harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1, node2, node3, RHEL10) using RabbitMQ 3.13.7 / Erlang 26.2.5.4 from the upstream packagecloud repos. Created a dedicated CA on node1 and issued per-node server certs plus a client cert. Each node's rabbitmq.conf disables plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp = none) and exposes AMQP only on 5671/TLS with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, enforcing that only clients presenting a certificate signed by the cluster CA can connect (verified both a successful mTLS handshake+AMQP publish/consume, and a hard TLS 'certificate_required' rejection for a client without a cert). The management HTTP API (15672) and inter-node/clustering ports (4369, 25672) are firewalled via firewalld rich rules to only accept traffic from the cluster's own /24 subnet, while 5671 is open cluster-wide for AMQP clients. All three nodes joined a single RabbitMQ cluster (rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows 3 running/disk nodes, no partitions). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured each node's boot_id and health baseline, restarted each node one at a time via `systemctl reboot` while the other two retained quorum, polled until each node's exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id (proving an actual reboot, not just a service restart), and re-verified cluster membership, TLS-only listener state, and a live client-cert-authenticated AMQP publish/consume after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 26.2.5.4 and RabbitMQ 3.13.7 on node1, node2, node3 via RabbitMQ team packagecloud repos (os=el dist=9 override for RHEL10)
Set up passwordless inter-node SSH using CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY for cert distribution

Generated a dedicated CA (CN=RabbitMQ Cluster CA, 10y validity) and per-node server certs with SAN DNS/IP entries, plus one client certificate, all on node1, and verified them against the CA with openssl verify
Distributed CA cert + node-specific server cert/key to node2 and node3 via scp, set ownership/perms to rabbitmq:rabbitmq
Configured /etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf on all 3 nodes: listeners.tcp=none, listeners.ssl.default=5671 with verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, TLS1.2/1.3 only, management.tcp on all interfaces
Generated and distributed a shared Erlang cookie to all nodes via secret_env
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin (offline) on all nodes, started and enabled rabbitmq-server via systemd
Opened firewalld ports: 5671/tcp open cluster-wide; 4369, 25672, 15672 restricted via rich rules to source 10.100.219.0/24 (cluster subnet) only
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster, confirmed 3-node cluster with no partitions
Created an AMQP user (appuser) with permissions, ran a Python/pika mTLS publish+consume test against all three nodes' 5671 ports using the CA-issued client cert, confirming cross-node routing
Verified TLS-layer and AMQP-layer rejection of connections lacking a valid client certificate (server ALERT: Certificate required; pika AMQPConnectionError)
Verified management HTTP API reachable from other cluster nodes (200) with no globally-open firewall rule

Executed mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + service state baseline per node, sequentially rebooted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified full cluster health, no partitions, TLS-only listener, and live client-cert AMQP connectivity after each restart before proceeding to the next node
Cleaned up transient test queue/vhost artifacts

evidence.summary: join_cluster succeeded for node2 and node3; rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all 3 as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with no network partitions

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS only (no plaintext listener)
evidence.summary: rabbitmq-diagnostics listeners shows only amqp/ssl on 5671 (no amqp/tcp 5672) on node1 both before and after all restarts

evidence.requirement: Cluster-created CA and certificates used for TLS
evidence.summary: Generated self-signed CA (CN=RabbitMQ Cluster CA) and per-node/client certs signed by it; openssl verify confirms all certs chain to the CA

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a CA-issued certificate are accepted (mutual TLS enforced)
evidence.summary: openssl s_client and rabbitmq broker log show 'SERVER ALERT: Fatal - Certificate required' for a connection without a client cert; pika test with the CA-issued client cert succeeds (publish+consume) while a pika test without a client cert fails with TLSV13_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: firewalld rich rules on all 3 nodes restrict ports 15672/25672/4369 to source 10.100.219.0/24 (the cluster subnet) only, with no unrestricted 'ports:' entry for 15672; curl from node1 to node2/node3 mgmt API returns 200 confirming intra-cluster reachability

Baseline boot_id 6ab6a71b...; systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; post-reboot boot_id changed to 92695d6f...; cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, no partitions; live mTLS AMQP publish/consume succeeded against node1 post-restart

Baseline boot_id 03408ac4...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; post-reboot boot_id changed to b14c5aa3...; cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running; mTLS AMQP publish/consume succeeded against node2 post-restart

Baseline boot_id 19062a82...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; post-reboot boot_id changed to 8ced0ed1...; rabbitmq-server became active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running; mTLS AMQP publish/consume succeeded against node3 post-restart
